title: KV shadow-prefix repro playbook
content:
Summary:
This is a personal playbook for reproducing a flaky issue we've been seeing in long-context runs where a stale/rotated KV prefix ("shadow prefix") is occasionally consulted by the attention kernel selection or KV index lookup, producing out-of-range lookups and garbled generations. Goal is to make a minimal, scriptable repro and a short mitigation checklist.

Context / observed symptoms:
- Failing requests are rare (~0.2% of long-context requests for a specific client test harness) and only appear after a long session (>8000 tokens).
- Symptoms: response truncation, occasional segfaults in custom attention kernel, logs show "kv_index: invalid slot 0xdeadbeef" or "kv_offset > seq_len - 1".
- Root suspicion: a rotated/evicted prefix buffer (shadow) is referenced due to an off-by-one in the KV rotation logic when handling wraparound + concurrent prefetch.

What I tried so far (chronological):
1) Smoke repro with python harness (local):
   - command: python3 tools/repro_kv_session.py --model rwinf-2b --seq 16384 --prefill 8200 --continuation 200 --seed 42
   - result: 0/100 fails locally (non-deterministic). Added verbose logs to KV manager.

2) Deterministic stress with single-threaded kernel on CPU (to remove race)
   - docker run --entrypoint bash -v $(pwd):/workspace repro:local -c "python3 tools/repro_kv_session.py --single-thread --repeat 500"
   - result: several reproductions seen. Logs show sequence of events: rotate->evict->read with same logical addresses.

3) Runtime traces:
   - Grepped logs for "kv_index"/"kv_offset" after repros. Example snippet: 
      [2025-11-04T14:12:03Z] kv-manager: rotate slot=7->11 seq_base=7800
      [2025-11-04T14:12:03Z] prefetcher: queued seq=7825 len=64
      [2025-11-04T14:12:03Z] attention-kernel: choosing kernel=fast_attn_v2 seq_len=128
      [2025-11-04T14:12:04Z] error: kv_index: invalid slot 2147483647 (0x7fffffff)
   - The invalid slot often equals large sentinel values, suggesting uninitialized memory read in the index table.

4) Bisected commit range for KV manager (last safe commit hash 3f1a2b -> first bad 4b7c9e). Notable changes: prefetch queue refactor (PR #1423).

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Race between prefetch enqueuer and rotate/evict path where we don't fence updates to the index table. On wrap, indices copied without atomic publish.
- H2: Off-by-one in circular buffer index math when seq_base crosses 8192/16384 boundary resulting in stale pointer as "shadow prefix".
- H3: Attention kernel selection uses an outdated cached seqlen distribution (cached key) and selects a kernel incompatible with current KV layout; kernel then reads wrong offsets.

Repro plan (minimal):
1) Build a minimal single-process harness that simulates: prefill -> streaming appends -> interleaved async prefetch -> explicit rotate at wrap threshold.
2) Add deterministic scheduler: use LIBCOOP_SLEEP hooks to force ordering permutations: (prefetch->rotate), (rotate->prefetch), (prefetch interrupted by rotate).
3) Run 10k permutations with ASAN/UBSAN (build with -fsanitize=address,undefined) and capture first failure.

Quick commands to run locally (notes):
- Build debug binary: make -C serving-runtime debug-kv SANITIZE=1 KERNEL=fast_attn_v2
- Run harness: ./build/debug/kv_repro --model=rwinf-2b --seed=99 --prefill=8200 --stream-ops=5000 --force-wrap=16384 --deterministic-schedule
- Tail logs with context: sed -n '1,300p' /tmp/kv_repro.log | grep -E "kv-?index|rotate|prefetch|invalid|segfault" -n

Key log snippets to capture on first failure (copy/paste format):
- KV manager rotate line with timestamps
- Prefetch queue snapshot: head/tail indexes
- Kernel choice snapshot: kernel name + cached seqlen + chosen path
- Backtrace (addr2line) of segfault if any

Quick patch ideas to test (non-invasive):
- Add seq fence: publish index table only after updating pointer (atomic store with release semantics). Try simple memory barrier in rotate path.
- In prefetch path, validate slot id before reading: if slot >= capacity or slot < 0 -> log and drop prefetch.
- Defensive kernel: if offset >= current_seq_len, fall back to safe kernel and log metric. (Can prevent crash while we patch bug.)

Rolling repro log example (fake but structurally similar):
--- start repro run 87 ---
[14:22:15.121] kv-manager: prefill complete seq_base=8200 capacity=16k
[14:22:17.511] prefetcher: push slot=12 seq=8224 len=64
[14:22:17.512] rotate: compute new_slot=0 old_base=8192 new_base=16384
[14:22:17.512] index-publish: table[0]=0x7f9b2c003010 (published)
[14:22:17.513] attention-kernel: chosen=fast_attn_v2 cached_seqlen=128 current_seqlen=132
[14:22:17.514] read-kv: slot=0 offset=131 -> read ok
[14:22:17.514] read-kv: slot=2147483647 offset=202 -> ERROR kv_index invalid slot
--- end repro run 87 ---

Data/metrics to collect when you reproduce:
- Histogram of slot ids used by kernels in last 1000 tokens before failure
- Counts of prefetch requests that targeted evicted slots
- Kernel switch events (timestamped) and the seqlen values that triggered selection
- Memory snapshots of index table immediately after rotate (hex dump small)

Investigation notes / ad-hoc findings:
- I instrumented index allocation with a generation counter; bad runs sometimes show generation mismatch (gen 42 read by kernel while table is being updated to gen 43). That points to missing memory fencing on publish.
- Adding a simple atomic flag around publish reduced repro rate from ~0.2% to 0.01% in my local stress runs. Encouraging but not definitive.

Mitigations (short-term):
- Ship defensive kernel fallback in Canary: if kernel sees out-of-range slot -> increment metric and switch to safe kernel. (safe kernel = slower but tolerates missing KV entries).
- Add validation in prefetch path to drop requests that reference slot < base or >= base+capacity with a logged metric.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Convert harness to run in CI with deterministic schedule permutations (ask infra for larger qemu timeout budgets).
- [ ] Draft PR with atomic publish + prefetch validation for quick canary. (PR draft id: repo/pr/??? )
- [ ] Add dashboard alert: 5xx rate for model rwinf-2b long-context > 0.05% -> trigger rollout with defensive kernel.
- [ ] Pair with Diego to run kernel trace with perf + pmap to watch for stale mappings.

Open questions / things to consider:
- Is attention kernel selection reading a stale cached seqlen from an allocator-global cache? Could be coming from an LRU cache per-thread not invalidated after rotate.
- Does dedicated autoscaling or shard migration ever cause temporary index pointer moves we didn't account for? (check Dedicated logs next).

Scratch area (commands I used while iterating):
- grep loop: for f in /tmp/kv_repro.*; do echo --- $f; tail -n 200 $f | grep -E "kv-manager|prefetch|rotate|index-publish|kv_index"; done
- reproducible run wrapper: nohup ./kv_repro --repeat=1000 --seed=1337 > /tmp/kv_repro.log 2>&1 &
- backtrace: gdb --batch -ex 'set pagination 0' -ex 'thread apply all bt full' --args ./kv_repro core.12345

Notes-to-self: Keep the harness small and deterministic. Prioritize fences + validation. If atomic publish eliminates repro consistently under stress, we ship that as quick fix and keep deeper refactor for next sprint.

End of notes (I'll iterate this doc as I get more deterministic traces).
